claims.text: Lawyers review a contract's legal terms, such as liability and applicable law, but some terms decide technical cost, which only the engineering team can estimate.

The data export term (what, format, when, also after the end) and how long the vendor keeps data before deleting it decide the cost of leaving; a contract that says nothing gives the team no written promise about format, window or deletion date.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 2; misconception 2; management.l3.vendor-lock-in five-line summary

claims.text: Notice before a vendor changes or retires an API version decides how often the team reworks its integration on someone else's schedule; a retired version is a breaking change for code calling it; 6 months usually leaves room in normal sprints, 1 month can force rework ahead of planned work.

Price changes at renewal, the term and its notice period decide whether a multi-year cost comparison still holds after the first year: a cap bounds later fees, no cap leaves them open; a short term can be read more than one way, so the reading relied on belongs in writing.

Table: export A CSV any time, B monthly, in writing: also after the end; retention A 90 days then delete + confirmation, B silent; API notice A 6 mo, B 1 mo; renewal A max +10%/yr, B no limit; term A 1 yr auto-renew 60 days notice, B 2 yrs 90 days; last row not 'Có'.
The evaluation says lawyers review the legal part, the team reads these terms itself because they decide technical cost, and the last column marks what must be in writing before signing.

Gateway B is ruled out at criterion T1, but its remaining rows are kept so a later evaluation need not redo them; every figure about the two gateways is assumed for illustration, not from a real vendor.
The team chose Gateway A for refunds in the first week of Sprint 15 (ADR 0010).
Only GatewayRefundClient knows the payment gateway's requests and answers, so a gateway API change means rewriting that class and its tests.
claims.source_hint: management.l3.vendor-lock-in five-line summary; ADR 0010 'Hệ quả' @ stage-3

claims.text: Try it: reading the cap as 10% of the previous year's fee, from 100 units year two is at most 110, year three 121; reading the 60 days as notice before the end of a term, notice must reach the vendor 60 days before year one ends or it renews. Both readings to confirm in writing.
With no limit on price changes at renewal, the fee after the first term cannot be bounded from the contract; a 2-year term with 90 days' notice binds the team longer before it can leave.
Asking for a term in writing before signing is a response that reduces a risk while it is still cheap.
